title: OpenAI's first hardware to ship by year-end? Supply chain says: Luxshare Precision is the exclusive manufacturer of the complete device, which looks like a doughnut

content_html:
According to supply chain sources cited today by National Business Daily, OpenAI's first AI hardware device is planned to begin shipping by the end of 2026, and Chinese manufacturers play a significant role in the project—Luxshare Precision not only exclusively handles final assembly, but also supplies core components. As for what the product actually looks like, OpenAI has remained tight-lipped.

Rumor: a "hockey puck" that can sense its environment Earlier reports sketched out the outline: the device is being developed by OpenAI together with LoveFrom, the studio of former Apple chief design officer Jony Ive. It reportedly looks much like a "donut," is about the size of a hockey puck, has no screen, and packs in microphones, speakers, cameras, and various environmental sensors. It focuses on voice interaction and can also sense its surroundings. Rumored pricing falls in the $300 to $400 range (about 2,004 to 2,672 yuan), but none of this has been officially confirmed.

Contract manufacturing rumors have reversed several times The rumor mill has not had a smooth ride either. In January this year, there were claims that the contract manufacturing order might shift from Luxshare Precision to Foxconn and be produced at a Vietnam factory; Luxshare later clarified the matter. OpenAI's global affairs chief Chris Lehane, however, has been consistent at the Davos forum in January: the company is "on track" to launch its first device in the second half of 2026.

Now that the supply chain has once again confirmed shipping at the end of the year, the day when ChatGPT moves from a chat box into a real-world object really seems close.
